items.claim: Prov.16.8 is rightly bounded alone, since it carries no divine-name token in any form (the row's actual warrant for breaking a 15:33-16:9 YHWH run at this verse) and neither neighboring verse shares a content root with it.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.8 contains no occurrence of the divine name in any form, bare or prefixed; oshb:Prov.16.7 and oshb:Prov.16.9 use unrelated vocabulary (derekh/ish; lev/adam) sharing no root with 16:8, so the single-verse boundary carries no undisclosed catchword pull from either side.

items.claim: The mishpat pairing of 16:10-16:11 is real, but the rejected_alternative is a strawman rival, since it only tests extending the pair forward into 16:12-16:15 rather than the stronger rival that 16:10 itself already carries the melekh token defining the following cluster while 16:11 does not.
items.evidence: 16:10's word מֶ֑לֶךְ (king) is the identical root cited by the next row's forms at 16:12-16:15; the root is present at Prov.16.10, absent at Prov.16.11, then present again at Prov.16.12 through Prov.16.15 -- a one-verse gap bracketed on both sides by the same token, not a clean forward-only boundary; this byte-true device straddles the row's own right seam without disclosure.

items.claim: The gap-free four-verse run description is accurate for 16:12-16:15 taken alone, but the rejected_alternative misstates why the wider span was cut, since it blames only 16:11's absence of the royal noun while lumping 16:10 into the same rejected six-verse span even though 16:10 independently carries the identical token the row uses to justify 16:12-16:15.
items.evidence: 16:10's word מֶ֑לֶךְ is the same royal-noun root as the row's own cited forms at 16:12-16:15; only 16:11 breaks the chain, yet the row's rejected_alternative treats the wider six-verse kings run as uniformly deficient by citing only 16:11's absence, without acknowledging that 16:10 independently meets the row's own inclusion criterion; the row's high confidence label does not account for this gap in the rival treatment.

items.claim: The 16:18-16:19 pairing is well-grounded, since both the ruach and ga'on/ge'im roots are shared in parallel slots, the inline ketiv before the qere is accurately disclosed, and the row's own device already tests and defensibly dismisses the adjacent tov echo to 16:20.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.18 and oshb:Prov.16.19 both carry ruach in the haughty/lowly-of-spirit slot and the pride root (ga'on/ge'im); the inline unpointed ketiv preceding the pointed qere at 16:19 matches the single kq note recorded for that verse in the inventory; neither 16:17 nor 16:20 shares a content root with 16:18 directly.

items.claim: 16:20 is correctly left standalone, since it shares no root with 16:21, and its own rejected_alternative already tests and defensibly dismisses the shared tov root with 16:19 on a real syntactic-function distinction.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.20 and oshb:Prov.16.21 share no content root; the tov token at 16:19 functions as the opening comparative of an antithetic line while at 16:20 it is the object of the opening clause, a real syntactic-function distinction rather than an asserted one.

items.claim: 16:24 is correctly bounded alone, since it shares no root with 16:23 or 16:25, and the non-adjacent bone/atsem echo to 15:30 is properly disclosed as texture rather than treated as a boundary driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.23 and oshb:Prov.16.25 share no root with oshb:Prov.16.24; the shared bone/atsem imagery with Prov.15.30 sits several verses away and is correctly kept out of the boundary argument as texture.

items.claim: The three-verse ish-opening construction run at 16:27-16:29 is real and correctly cut against 16:26, but the claim that the run breaks cleanly at 16:30 is overstated, since 16:30 recycles the same rare tahpukhot noun used inside the cluster at 16:28, an undisclosed echo straddling the row's own right seam.
items.evidence: ish plus a construct-genitive vice-noun opens Prov.16.27 through Prov.16.29 in immediate succession, and 16:30 opens with a participle instead, so the grammatical template genuinely stops there as the row states; but תַּ֭הְפֻּכוֹת (16:28) and תַּהְפֻּכ֑וֹת (16:30) are the same noun, and the root is rare book-wide (9 of 915 verses per a skeleton sweep); its recurrence one verse past the row's own boundary is a byte-true device the row does not disclose, so the breaks-cleanly framing overstates the seam even though the ish template itself is correctly bounded, and the row's high confidence label does not register this gap.

items.claim: 16:33 is correctly left standalone, since it shares no root with 16:32, and the non-adjacent mishpat/mishpato echo back to 16:10-16:11 is properly disclosed as texture rather than a boundary driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.16.32 shares no content root with oshb:Prov.16.33; the rejected_alternative accurately states no shared token links 16:32's self-mastery saying to 16:33's lot-and-YHWH saying, and the mishpato/mishpat echo back to 16:10-16:11 is correctly kept out of the boundary argument as non-adjacent texture.
